sentences.text: Soriatitan golmayensis is known from a single species found in the Golmayo Formation, with remains including a tooth, several vertebrae, limb bones, and pelvic fragments.
Until this dinosaur was found, scientists believed that brachiosaurids had gone extinct in Europe about 130 million years ago.
The only known specimen was discovered in the Golmayo Formation in Soria province, Spain, specifically within the Zorralbo 1 deposit.
Excavation of the fossil began in 2000 by a team of paleontologists from Soria province, and preparation started in 2009 with help from the Dinópolis Foundation.
This adult herbivore possessed small teeth measuring only 18 millimeters in length, indicating a diet of soft vegetation.
Like its relatives Cedarosaurus, Tastavinsaurus, and Venenosaurus, it featured anterior-middle neural spines that were inclined forward.
The animal reached a full size of 13 to 14 meters and weighed nearly 8 tons.
Cladistic analysis places Soriatitan in the family Brachiosauridae within the superfamily Titanosauriformes.
Soriatitan lived during the Early Cretaceous, between 138 and 129 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
Fossilized plant remains suggest the environment was subtropical and dominated by conifer trees, which were likely its main food source.
